items.title: How close can pure functional programming get to C?
items.contentSnippet:
Article URL: https://rtfeldman.com/fp-vs-c
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50218195
Points: 232
# Comments: 67
items.creator: stmonty

summaries.zh: 文章探讨了纯函数式编程（FP）与C语言在性能和接近程度上的对比。作者认为，通过优化和特定技术，FP可以接近C的性能，但需要更多努力。文章指出FP在抽象和表达力上优于C，但在底层控制和效率上稍逊。总结来说，FP在保持高抽象的同时，通过优化可接近C的性能，但两者在应用场景和特点上存在差异。
summaries.en: The article explores how close pure functional programming (FP) can approach C's performance and efficiency. It discusses the trade-offs between FP and C, such as FP's emphasis on immutability and higher-order functions versus C's low-level control and direct memory management. The piece highlights that while FP can achieve near-C speeds with optimized libraries and compilers, it may require more effort to leverage full hardware capabilities. The author concludes that FP can be competitive with C in many scenarios but may not always match its raw performance without significant optimization.

items.summary: 文章探讨了纯函数式编程（FP）与C语言在性能和接近程度上的对比。作者认为，通过优化和特定技术，FP可以接近C的性能，但需要更多努力。文章指出FP在抽象和表达力上优于C，但在底层控制和效率上稍逊。总结来说，FP在保持高抽象的同时，通过优化可接近C的性能，但两者在应用场景和特点上存在差异。

summaries.zh: 《1978年“自然语言编程”的愚蠢之处》一文指出，自然语言编程因缺乏精确性和逻辑性而不可行。作者认为，自然语言易含歧义，难以实现可靠计算。文章强调编程需严谨定义，而非依赖模糊的自然语言。该观点引发广泛讨论，体现自然语言与形式化语言的差异。
summaries.en: The article "The foolishness of 'natural language programming'" (1978) criticizes the idea of using natural language for programming, arguing it is impractical and inefficient. The author, Edsger Dijkstra, highlights the limitations of human language in precision and ambiguity compared to formal programming languages. He emphasizes the need for clear, unambiguous communication in programming, advocating for structured, mathematical approaches. The piece reflects on the challenges of translating natural language into executable code and suggests it would lead to confusion and errors. Dijkstra's perspective underscores the importance of discipline and rigor in software development.

summaries.en: Fable 5.1 uses steganography to hide messages in images by embedding data within the file's metadata without altering its visual appearance. The process involves encoding text into binary and embedding it into the image's least significant bits, ensuring the change is imperceptible. This technique allows for secure communication by concealing information within seemingly ordinary images. The article explores the technical details of how this works, including the methods and tools used for both embedding and extracting hidden messages.

items.title: Ask HN: If the models are so good, why doesn't OpenAI just start 100 companies?
items.content:
Title is a bit of an exaggeration but the question is more: if the frontier models are so good, why even sell them as your primary money maker?

Couldn't OpenAI or Anthropic make a lot more money by just starting companies themselves that leverage the models and building their own products?

Is selling tokens really the best strategy?

Especially with commodification and prices declining wouldn't that indicate there is more money to be made on the application-side of the models rather than the utility side
